text:
jordan: FYI found a privacy bug in Console — dashboard widget shows metrics from another project while I'm scoped to project X. happened when I opened widget then used quick-switch to Y. repro in staging.

nina: oh no. which widget? is it the shared activity-timeline or the insights sparkline?

jordan: the activity-timeline. it displayed events with project Y ids in the row details even though header X was set. i think it started after we rolled the shared-widget-cache change last week.

leo: shared-widget-cache? that was supposed to reduce cold loads by memoizing widget queries keyed by user_id + widget_type. did we forget project_id in the key? :grimacing:

jordan: i looked quickly — redis keys look like `widget:uid:activity-timeline` with no project. so yep. quick repro:
```bash
# in staging
export TOKEN=...
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Project-Id: X" "https://staging.console.internal/api/widget/activity"
# switch project fast in UI to Y and call same api with header Y
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Project-Id: Y" "https://staging.console.internal/api/widget/activity"
```
first response sometimes returns cached payload for X when header is Y.

tanya: that explains a ticket i saw from support. could be bad if some orgs have overlapping users. high severity. we should rollback the cache or at least change cache key.

nina: agreed. quick mitigation: patch cache key to include project id and add an expiring prefix for the next hour. longer term: decide whether cache should be per-user-per-project or per-project-global depending on widget semantics.

leo: small debate point: some widgets are cross-project summaries (we intentionally cache globally), others are per-project. we need metadata on widget registration `cache_scope: project|global` so the cache behaviour is explicit. right now registration defaults to global.

jordan: can we hotfix by making activity-timeline project-scoped? i can open PR. also do we have telemetry that can surface these mismatches?

nina: add a metric `widget_cache_scope_mismatch` emitted when cache hits and header-project != cached_project_id. payload: [widget, cached_project_id, requested_project_id, pod]. even a counter will help triage.

leo: i'm also worried about edge cases at routing layer: if a request goes to a pod that hasn't rolled the key fix it might write the wrong key. can we set a short TTL and invalidate existing keys on rollout?

tanya: plan: (1) nina to push metric and alert (2) jordan to open PR changing activity-timeline cache scope to project and include migration note (3) leo to run redis key scan and schedule invalidation for any `widget:uid:activity*` mismatches (4) deploy strategy: small canary -> immediate rollback if mismatch rate > 0.1%

deploy-bot: deployment started: staging/widget-cache-fix v2026.7 -> 4 pods. CI checks passed.

nina: added temporary grafana panel: `widget_cache_scope_mismatch / minute` and alert `>=1 in 5m` to #incidents. link: https://grafana.staging/redwood/d/abcd/widgets (pasted)

jordan: i ran redis scan and found ~120 keys missing project suffix; scheduled TTL purge for 5m. also added e2e that rapid-switches projects then asserts widget response project ids match request header. will include in canary gate.

leo: i'll follow up with a PR to add `cache_scope` field to widget registry and update docs. also audit other caches for missing namespace keys (quota caches, prefetch caches).

tanya: thanks. let's keep this high priority, especially before the next prod rollout. tagging @oncall-sre just in case we need to escalate.

jordan: thanks all, will post PR link shortly and update once keys are purged. :thumbsup:
